crossRefs.note: “Be silent! Leave me alone, that I may speak. Let come on me what will.
Mark well, Job, and listen to me. Hold your peace, and I will speak.
I am like one who is a joke to his neighbor, I, who called on God, and he answered. The just, the blameless man is a…
In the thought of him who is at ease there is contempt for misfortune. It is ready for them whose foot slips.
Is it good that he should search you out? Or as one deceives a man, will you deceive him?
They have gaped on me with their mouth. They have struck me on the cheek reproachfully. They gather themselves together…
My friends scoff at me. My eyes pour out tears to God,
Surely there are mockers with me. My eye dwells on their provocation.

translations.web: Allow me, and I also will speak; After I have spoken, mock on.
translations.bsb: Bear with me while I speak; then, after I have spoken, you may go on mocking.
translations.kjv: Suffer me that I may speak; and after that I have spoken, mock on.
translations.asv: Suffer me, and I also will speak; And after that I have spoken, mock on.
